text:
Kathy Castor highlights legislative priorities including EARLY Act passage and tech accountability
U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor, currently representing Florida’s 14th district in Congress, announced on social media a series of legislative actions she has undertaken, including the passage of the EARLY Act and progress on the Ratepayer Protection Act.
On July 21, 2026, Castor posted about her bipartisan efforts with Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz: "My bipartisan EARLY Act with @RepDWSTweets has PASSED the House! Detecting cancer earlier saves lives. This bill reauthorizes critical outreach initiatives that help women understand their risks, advocate for their health and get the tools they need to beat cancer. I’m proud".
Later that day, Castor addressed consumer protection and technology accountability: "We’re holding Big Tech accountable and protecting consumers. Thanks to bipartisan support, my Ratepayer Protection Act is headed to a vote on the House floor! Across the board, I’m fighting to lower costs and keep your hard-earned dollars in your pocket."
On July 22, 2026, she commented on federal spending, "The Big Ugly Bill will add $3.4 trillion to the deficit by 2034. One of the most expensive bills ever passed. Now, extreme politicians want to dig the hole deeper and add another $95 billion to help fund a war Americans do not support. I am fighting to lower health care costs,".
Castor has served as U.S. Representative for Florida’s 14th District since 2007 after succeeding Jim Davis. She previously held office in the Florida House of Representatives and was born in Miami in 1966 before moving to Tampa where she currently resides. Her educational background includes a BA from Emory University (1988) and a JD from Florida State University (1991).
